data.description:
## Context
After `rebar verify-completion antiutopic-toadyish-goldfinch --ref 48d4a4d4a984cca201bbbb6874e4e8500a729d3a` produced a signed PASS, `rebar transition ... closed --ref=48d4a4d4a984cca201bbbb6874e4e8500a729d3a` launched the completion verifier again instead of reusing the ticket's already-recorded attested PASS for the identical immutable ref. The duplicate provider run added several minutes and unnecessary model cost to a close whose verified material had not changed.

## Expected behavior
A close operation should reuse a ticket's current, certifiable, attested PASS when its `verified_at_sha` exactly matches the commit resolved by the close operation's `--ref`, provided the attestation is otherwise valid for the ticket and required verification scope. It must run a new completion verification when the ref resolves differently, the attestation is stale/invalid, the scope differs, or no qualifying PASS exists.

## Investigation plan
- Reproduce standalone verification followed by close at the same immutable SHA and instrument provider invocation count.
- Trace the close-gate attestation lookup and ref-resolution paths to prove why the existing PASS is ignored.
- Add a held-out regression test that observes one provider call across verify-then-close at the same SHA.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for ref drift, invalid signatures, scope mismatch, and failed/non-certifiable verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Closing a ticket at the exact SHA of an existing valid attested PASS does not invoke the completion provider again.
- [ ] The close records or references valid completion evidence for that exact SHA.
- [ ] A changed ref/commit forces a fresh verification.
- [ ] Invalid, failed, non-certifiable, or scope-incompatible attestations force a fresh verification.
- [ ] CLI behavior is covered end-to-end for explicit `--ref`.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, and typecheck pass.
data.title: Reuse same-ref attested completion verification during close
